To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) GRIN lens position tolerance is the most critical issue for the OCT imaging performance, which needs to controlled within 0,1 mm to achieve a WD longer than 3 mm and lateral resolution better than 25 μm; (2) the radius of curvature tolerance of MEMS mirror is not a critical design issue for endoscopic OCT probe design; and (3) astigmatism introduced to OCT image by cylindrical plastic tubing is not a critical issue.

the radius of curvature for MEMS mirror should be larger than 200 mm, and the optical assembly tolerance should be controlled within 1 mm for WD greater than 3.0 mm and lateral resolution less than 25 μm. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a 0.1- mm tolerance in fiber to GRIN distance, a 200-mm radius of curvature of mirrors, and a cylindrical plastic tubing with an outer diameter of 1 mm and length of 3-5 mm would be sufficient for a MEMS based OCT endoscopic imaging probe.

the optical alignment inside the probe needs to be controlled to within 0.05 mm, the GRIN lens and the fiber tip need to be aligned within 0.2 mm, and the MEMS mirror should have a radius of curvature greater than 200 μm to avoid the influence on the imaging performance.
a 3.5-mm WD can be achieved with a 1-mm-diameter OCT probe, and the lateral resolution is about 25 μm, which is sufficient for clinical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OCT endoscopic probe design should be carefully optimized with respect to the imaging performance requirements.
the optical alignment accuracy is critical in the design of OCT endoscopes.
the OCT endoscopic imaging is sensitive to the optical alignment and design of the imaging probe, especially the GRIN lens position and the radius of curvature for the MEMS mirror surface.
